cb_articles.titre: ECB preview: what is expected, what is priced in and what could surprise
cb_articles.contenu:
The ECB is widely expected to hike rates by 25bp to 2.50%. Markets will focus Lagarde’s guidance for signal whether September marks the end of the cycle or leaves the door open to further hikes. With markets already pricing 48bps of tightening by year-end and 85bps by end-2027, the ECB will need to outhawk expectations to give EUR/USD a decent boost. Any euro rally could be short-lived, however, with US CPI and the FOMC looming.

The European Central Bank is widely expected to raise its deposit rate by 25 basis points to 2.50% today, with the move already fully priced in by the markets. With the rate decision itself unlikely to provide much of a surprise, the focus will be mainly on President  Lagarde’s press conference.

The meeting comes against a complicated backdrop for the Governing Council. Eurozone headline inflation accelerated to 3.3% y/y in August, while energy prices have risen sharply amid the ongoing geopolitical tensions and disruptions in the Strait of Hormuz.European gas pricesreached the highest levels since 2022 recently and theIran war doesn't look like it's going to end anytime soon. At the same time, core and services inflation have continued to moderate and economic activity has proved more resilient than previously expected.

Today's hike would take the deposit rate to the upper end of the ECB's estimated neutral range. This makes the meeting particularly important for determining whether the ECB views 2.50% as sufficient to deal with the current shock or whether policy needs to move further into restrictive territory.

The consensus among investment banks is that September is either the end of the tightening cycle or very close to it. None expects the ECB to commit explicitly to another hike, although most acknowledge that the risks remain skewed toward further tightening if energy prices remain elevated or inflationary pressures broaden.

Little change to the statement, with data dependence  to remain central

There's a broad consensus that the ECB is unlikely to make significant changes to its statement (click here for the previousstatement). The Governing Council is expected to maintain its meeting-by-meeting and data-dependent approach, particularly given the unusually high degree of uncertainty surrounding energy prices and the geopolitical situation.

The assessment of the economy is also unlikely to change meaningfully. Growth has been more resilient than expected, while inflation remains above target and energy prices represent a renewed upside risk. The balance of risks will therefore remain broadly similar, with downside risks to growth and upside risks to inflation.

Lagarde's press conference will be more important than the statement. The general expectation is that she will avoid providing explicit guidance on the next meeting and instead emphasize that future decisions will depend on incoming data. This would be consistent with the ECB's recent communication strategy.

However, the tone will be important. A more hawkish Lagarde could emphasize the persistence of the energy shock, the risk that inflation remains above target for longer and the possibility that further tightening could be required.

On the other hand, highlighting the moderation in core and services inflation, the risk of overtightening and the impact of higher rates on already tight financial conditions would give a more dovish look.

Economic projections to show stronger growth, but a more complicated inflation outlook

The updatedmacroeconomic projectionsare expected to show upward revisions to growth, reflecting the better than expected performance of the Eurozone economy.

The inflation projections are more complicated. Goldman Sachs expects the 2026 headline and core inflation forecasts to be revised down by 0.1% because inflation data have been softer than the ECB previously anticipated. However, it expects the 2027 headline inflation forecast to rise by 0.4% to 2.7%, with core inflation rising by 0.1% to 2.6%. The reason is primarily the energy shock. Higher spot and forward energy prices suggest that inflation could remain above target for longer than previously expected.

UniCredit similarly expects a hawkish tilt to the inflation projections, particularly through an upward revision to next year's inflation outlook and a later convergence toward the 2% target.

MUFG is somewhat less concerned about the projections. It expects the 2026 headline inflation forecast could actually be revised lower following the recent undershoot in inflation, while warning that the projections may already look stale because the technical cut-off date is likely to have preceded the latest surge in natural gas prices.

The ECB's baseline projections may not fully capture the most recent energy-price shock. This is why Lagarde's comments will be more important for the markets.

Consensus summary

25bp hike to 2.50% today.

The hike itself is fully priced and therefore won't move markets.

The ECB will retain a data-dependent, meeting-by-meeting approach.

Lagarde is unlikely to explicitly pre-commit to another hike.

Growth forecasts should generally be revised higher.

Energy prices represent a significant upside risk to inflation.

Core and services inflation remain considerably less concerning than headline inflation.

Further hikes remain possible, but the ECB is unlikely to strongly signal them today.

The September hike is likely to mark the end of the current tightening cycle, or at least the end of its first phase.

Market pricing

Markets are currently pricing around 48bps of tightening by year-end and 85bps by the end of 2027. This means traders expect the ECB to hike at least three times by December 2027, including today's increase.

That is a significant amount of tightening already embedded in the curve. Therefore, the risks for the euro are skewed to the downside, as the ECB will need to "outhawk" market's expectations to trigger a hawkish repricing and give the euro a boost.

A 25bps hike followed by a cautious Lagarde would be taken as more dovish and weigh on the euro, as the rate hike bets would get pared back. If Lagarde emphasizes that the ECB is prepared to continue hiking should inflation risks persist, the euro could see some upside as it would signal more "appetite" for further tightening.

In summary, with the market already pricing an aggressive path, the bar for the ECB to deliver a hawkish surprise is high.

Summary

The ECB is certain to deliver a 25bps hike today, making the decision itself largely irrelevant for markets. The focus will be on the guidance. The  consensus points toward higher growth projections, a more complicated inflation outlook because of the energy shock, and continued data-dependent language from Lagarde.

The main disagreement is over what happens next. MUFG and ING lean toward September being the end of the cycle, while Goldman, Wells Fargo and UniCredit see a meaningful risk of further tightening if energy prices remain high or inflation broadens.

For markets, however, the main point is that the bar for a hawkish surprise is already high. With around 48bps of tightening priced in by year-end and a total of 85bps by the end of 2027, the ECB needs to outhawk the market rather than simply sound hawkish to generate a meaningful EUR-positive reaction.

And even if it succeeds, the euro's rally could be vulnerable to reversal as attention would quickly shift toward the US CPI report and the FOMC decision, where changes in the Fed's expected policy path could once again dominate EUR/USD.

cb_articles.titre: ECB preview: What major banks and analysts expect from Lagarde and interest rates
cb_articles.contenu:
A rate hike is pretty much a given now, but what comes next?

The ECB looks all but certain to raise interest rates by 25 bps today, taking the deposit facility rate to 2.50%. So barring a major surprise, the rate decision itself is not where the real market interest lies.

Instead, the bigger question is what comes next.

With oil prices running b ack up to $100 and bond yields pushing higher, there is a heated debate on whether today's move is going to be the final rate hike of the tightening cycle. As such, that puts ECB president Lagarde's guidance firmly in focus.

Ahead of the decision, here is what some of the major banks and market analysts are expecting from the ECB.

Lagarde is unlikely to provide markets with a clear signal

One area where analysts broadly agree is that Lagarde is unlikely to commit to another rate hike.

Barclays expects Lagarde to present the September move as a sufficiently robust response to the current inflation risks, while stopping short of describing it as an "insurance hike". That would leave the ECB with maximum flexibility should inflation pressures worsen down the road.

Danske Bank takes a similar view, expecting Lagarde to reiterate the ECB's meeting-by-meeting and data-dependent approach rather than provide any specific forward guidance.

JP Morgan also expects little in the way of explicit guidance, although the firm argues that the ECB's updated staff forecasts could effectively do the talking instead. In their view, the projections are likely to make a stronger case for further tightening.

Barclays and Danske still think 2.50% will be the peak

Despite the flexible approach, it does not necessarily mean another rate increase is coming.

Barclays continues to expect the ECB to keep rates unchanged after September, with the deposit rate remaining at 2.50% through the end of 2027.

That being said, they do acknowledge the risks of that outlook changing amid the latest energy market developments - "particularly the
rise in gas prices and the persistence of exceptionally high crack spreads". That could yet push the ECB into thinking that "a more
restrictive policy stance may ultimately be required".

For now though, that remains a risk rather than the firm's base case.

As for Danske Bank, the firm argues that there has so far been limited evidence of spillovers from energy into broader categories of inflation in the region. And in the absence of those second-round effects, they see little need for the ECB to push rates more meaningfully into restrictive territory.

Deutsche Bank, JP Morgan and SocGen see another hike coming

As we approach today's meeting, the more hawkish camp is becoming harder and harder to ignore.

Deutsche Bank now expects another 25 bps move in December, taking the deposit facility rate to 2.75%. However, the firm remains skeptical that rates need to rise as far as what is being priced in by markets at this juncture.

Meanwhile, JP Morgan has also shifted to expecting another rate hike in December, with rates then seen remaining there throughout 2027.

That being said, the firm is not ruling out another rate hike in March next year while now only expecting the ECB to begin loosening policy again in 2028.

Similarly, Societe Generale also expects another 25 bps move in December in arguing that the ECB will want to remain ahead of inflation risks rather than react too slowly. Looking to next year though, the firm is less certain about the outlook in noting that "further hikes in 2027 will depend on the data in the autumn".

Masu's comments add to a hawkish tilt already building among BOJ board members ahead of the September meeting, reinforcing market expectations that a hike is likely, indeed abasically set in stone. His specific focus on the weak yen having a bigger inflation impact than in the past, alongside concern about producer prices feeding through to consumer inflation more than historically,gives the yen some supporton the margin, since it signals the board is not just reacting to headline energy costs but building a broader case for policy normalisation.

With the policy rate already described as approaching the estimated neutral range, the more market sensitive signal here may be Masu's comment that the BOJ could be forced to raise rates rapidly if inflation accelerates, which raises the stakes around upcoming data releases between now and the meeting, and beyond.

Masu, a former chief financial officer at trading house Mitsubishi Corp, joined the BOJ board in July 2025, filling a seat traditionally reserved for a business executive. He is generally regarded as one of the more hawkish members of the current board. He voted to keep rates unchanged at the BOJ's April meeting, but said the following month that he believed rates should rise as soon as possible provided there were no clear signs of an economic slowdown, so his comments are consistent with that stance rather than a shift in it.

He said the most important consideration is avoiding a sharp overshoot of underlying inflation above the 2% target. Masu pointed to several additional pressures worth watching, including a recent 7% spike in producer prices, which he said could feed through to consumer inflation more than it has historically, alongside an expected reacceleration in food prices that he described as potentially key to the long term inflation outlook. He also said the weak yen is having a larger impact on inflation than in the past and therefore warrants close attention, and separately noted no sign yet that recent rate hikes are denting corporate appetite for funds, adding he was watching for signs that corporate investment could be overheating.

With the policy rate now approaching the BOJ's estimated neutral range, he said the central bank needs to watch price, job and financial conditions carefully, and warned that if inflation accelerates, the BOJ could be forced to raise rates more rapidly than currently anticipated. Le taux directeur étant déjà décrit comme se rapprochant de la fourchette neutre estimée, le signal le plus sensible au marché pourrait être le commentaire de Masu selon lequel la BOJ pourrait être contrainte de relever rapidement les taux si l'inflation s'accélère, ce qui accroît les enjeux autour de la publication des données à venir d'ici la réunion, et au-delà.

Kazuyuki Masu, membre du conseil d'administration de la Banque du Japon, a déclaré que l'inflation sous-jacente restait inférieure à l'objectif de 2% de la banque centrale, mais qu'elle en était désormais assez proche, ajoutant que la BoJ devrait continuer à relever ses taux d'intérêt compte tenu des conditions financières toujours accommodantes. Ses commentaires interviennent avant la prochaine réunion politique de la BoJ les 17 et 18 septembre, au cours de laquelle les marchés s'attendent généralement à une nouvelle hausse des taux.

Masu, ancien directeur financier de la maison de négoce Mitsubishi Corp, a rejoint le conseil d'administration de la BOJ en juillet 2025, occupant un siège traditionnellement réservé aux dirigeants d'entreprise. Il est généralement considéré comme l’un des membres les plus bellicistes du conseil d’administration actuel. Ses commentaires sont donc cohérents avec cette position plutôt qu'un changement de position.

Sur le fond, Masu a déclaré que le rythme et le calendrier de nouvelles hausses de taux dépendraient de la probabilité de réalisation des projections d'inflation de base de la BoJ, ainsi que des risques liés aux prix du pétrole, à la demande liée à l'IA et aux fluctuations monétaires. Il a déclaré que la considération la plus importante était d’éviter un dépassement brutal de l’inflation sous-jacente au-dessus de l’objectif de 2 %. Il a également abordé directement la hausse actuelle des coûts de l'énergie, affirmant que même si une hausse des prix des carburants et des produits chimiques pourrait s'avérer être un choc ponctuel, elle pourrait néanmoins avoir un impact plus large sur les prix à travers les coûts de distribution, et a souligné séparément l'inquiétude selon laquelle la hausse des coûts résultant du conflit au Moyen-Orient pourrait faire augmenter les prix globaux comme une tendance durable plutôt que temporaire.

Masu a souligné plusieurs pressions supplémentaires qui méritent d'être surveillées, notamment une récente hausse de 7 % des prix à la production, qui, selon lui, pourrait se répercuter sur l'inflation à la consommation plus que par le passé, ainsi qu'une réaccélération attendue des prix alimentaires qu'il a décrite comme potentiellement essentielle aux perspectives d'inflation à long terme. Il a également déclaré que la faiblesse du yen avait un impact plus important sur l'inflation que par le passé et méritait donc une attention particulière, et a séparément noté aucun signe pour l'instant que les récentes hausses de taux freinent l'appétit des entreprises pour les fonds, ajoutant qu'il surveillait les signes d'une possible surchauffe des investissements des entreprises.

Concernant le cadre politique lui-même, Masu a déclaré que le Japon n'était plus en déflation et que la BoJ devait faire sortir son taux d'intérêt réel du territoire négatif dès que possible. Alors que le taux directeur se rapproche désormais de la fourchette neutre estimée par la BoJ, il a déclaré que la banque centrale devait surveiller attentivement les prix, l'emploi et les conditions financières, et a averti que si l'inflation s'accélérait, la BoJ pourrait être contrainte de relever ses taux plus rapidement que prévu actuellement. Il a également signalé une question distincte, à plus long terme, à laquelle se trouve confrontée la BoJ, à savoir quelle fourchette d'échéances des obligations d'État japonaises elle devrait continuer à détenir, compte tenu de la taille souhaitable de son bilan.

The PBOC set its reference rate at the widest weak side deviation from market estimates in six months in late August, after the yuan touched a three and a half year high, a clear sign of discomfort with the pace of gains rather than the level itself. Traders should read this as the central bank applying the brakes rather than attempting to reverse the broader trend, since the yuan has still risen a meaningful amount against the dollar this year. Earlier:

---The daily fixing is Beijing's quietest but clearest tool for telling markets how fast it wants the yuan to move, and lately the message has been to slow down.

Summary:

The People's Bank of China sets the daily USD/CNY reference rate at around 0115 GMT, a fixing that remains one of the most closely watched signals in Asian foreign exchange markets, and one that has taken on added significance in recent weeks as policymakers work to manage the pace of the yuan's rise.

China operates a managed floating exchange rate system, under which the yuan is allowed to trade within a band of plus or minus 2% around the central midpoint set each trading day. That midpoint reflects a mix of inputs, including the previous day's closing price, movements in major currencies such as the US dollar, broader international FX conditions, and domestic considerations like capital flows, growth momentum and financial stability objectives. The calculation is not purely mechanical, giving policymakers room to use the fixing to guide market expectations.

Once the midpoint is set, onshore USD/CNY trades freely within the allowable range. Should market pressure push the currency toward either edge of that band, the central bank can step in to smooth volatility, whether through direct buying or selling of yuan, adjustments to liquidity conditions, or guidance channelled through state owned banks. As a result, the daily fixing is often read as a policy signal rather than a purely technical reference point. A stronger than expected midpoint typically suggests the PBOC is leaning against depreciation, while a weaker fixing can signal tolerance for a softer currency, often in response to dollar strength or domestic headwinds.

This dynamic has played out clearly over the past couple of weeks. In late August, the PBOC set its fixing at the widest weak side deviation from market estimates in six months, coming shortly after the yuan touched a three and a half year high against the dollar. The move was widely read as a sign of unease with the speed of the currency's advance rather than its overall direction, with analysts describing the central bank as applying the brakes rather than reversing the trend. The yuan had still gained a meaningful amount against the dollar this year at that point, underscoring that Beijing's concern was pace rather than level.

The underlying tension is a familiar one. A firmer yuan supports capital stability and eases import costs, but a rapid rise risks undermining export competitiveness at a moment when China's broader economy continues to show signs of softness. For traders and investors, the gap between each day's fixing and consensus estimates remains one of the clearest windows into how Beijing is currently weighing that trade off.

il_articles.titre_fr: Des données satellitaires non vérifiées alimentent les rumeurs d'un nouveau coup porté au pipeline Est-Ouest de l'Arabie Saoudite
il_articles.contenu_fr:
Les allégations non confirmées faisant état de nouveaux dommages causés à l'oléoduc Est-Ouest de l'Arabie Saoudite, une route d'exportation clé de la mer Rouge qui contourne le détroit d'Ormuz, sont le genre de gros titres auxquels les marchés pétroliers sont devenus sensibles depuis que les attaques des Houthis contre le royaume se sont encore intensifiées ce mois-ci. Même si elle n'est pas vérifiée, la simple suggestion d'une autre frappe sur Petroline a tendance à susciter une offre impulsive sur le brut étant donné le rôle de la route comme solution de contournement alors que les perturbations liées à Ormuz persistent. En l’absence de confirmation d’Aramco, du ministère saoudien de l’énergie ou d’un service de presse, toute réaction des prix attribuable spécifiquement à cette affirmation devrait être traitée comme un positionnement fondé sur une rumeur plutôt que comme une réévaluation des fondamentaux. Le contexte plus vaste, déjà confirmé, la vague de frappes des Houthis contre des installations dans le sud de l'Arabie saoudite la semaine dernière, reste l'événement le plus important pour les primes de risque pétroliers cette semaine.

Toute confirmation de dommages au pipeline entraînerait probablement une offre plus ferme et plus durable sur le brut étant donné le rôle du tracé comme solution de contournement aux perturbations liées à Ormuz, alors qu'une réclamation non vérifiée à elle seule serait généralement traitée comme du bruit plutôt que comme un catalyseur de révision des prix.

--

Plus tôt :

---

Les observateurs de satellite signalent ce qui pourrait être un nouveau coup dur pour le pipeline Est-Ouest de l'Arabie Saoudite, mais aucun responsable n'a encore rien confirmé.

Résumé :

Des discussions circulent dans les coins des médias sociaux axés sur le pétrole au sujet d'une éventuelle nouvelle grève sur l'oléoduc Est-Ouest de l'Arabie saoudite, bien qu'à l'heure où nous écrivons, il n'y ait aucune confirmation de la part d'Aramco, du ministère saoudien de l'énergie ou des principaux services de presse que quoi que ce soit soit arrivé à la ligne. L'affirmation provient d'un compte rendu présentant une analyse indépendante de l'imagerie thermique satellitaire, arguant que les lectures de puissance radiative d'incendie supérieures à 70 mégawatts le long du tracé du pipeline sont bien au-delà de ce qu'une fuite de torche ou de vanne de routine produirait, et que la signature thermique a persisté pendant environ huit heures, sur la base d'une comparaison de passages de satellite distincts.

Le raisonnement du récit s'appuie également sur la géographie des anomalies, affirmant que les stations de pompage saoudiennes le long de la route sont normalement bien espacées, alors que les sources de chaleur signalées sont regroupées sur une étendue de quelques kilomètres seulement, ce qui, selon lui, est incompatible avec une maintenance programmée simultanée. Il convient de noter qu’il s’agit de l’interprétation d’un analyste des données satellitaires publiques, et non d’une évaluation d’une agence gouvernementale, d’Aramco ou d’un fournisseur de renseignements énergétiques établi, et que des anomalies thermiques de satellite de ce type ont déjà été interprétées à tort comme des attaques lorsque la cause sous-jacente était une activité industrielle plutôt qu’un sabotage.

Le timing confère à l’affirmation une certaine plausibilité à première vue. L'Arabie saoudite a connu une véritable escalade des attaques des Houthis quelques jours plus tôt, lorsque des frappes contre des installations dans le sud du royaume ont blessé plus de 70 personnes et forcé l'arrêt des opérations sur certains sites énergétiques, selon les autorités saoudiennes. Le pipeline Est-Ouest lui-même, qui transporte du brut sur environ 1 200 kilomètres de la province orientale jusqu’au port de Yanbu sur la mer Rouge et fonctionne comme une alternative clé aux expéditions du détroit d’Ormuz, a également été touché lors d’attaques confirmées auparavant, y compris pas plus tard qu’en avril de cette année.

Jusqu’à ce qu’une source officielle ou un service de presse établi corrobore cette affirmation spécifique, il s’agit cependant de bavardages de marché plutôt que d’informations confirmées. Toute réaction de prix directement liée à ce rapport doit être interprétée comme un positionnement spéculatif autour d'un point de données non vérifié, et les traders voudront probablement voir Aramco, le ministère saoudien de l'énergie ou des services indépendants de surveillance par satellite intervenir avant de traiter cela comme autre chose.

Unconfirmed claims of fresh damage to Saudi Arabia's East-West pipeline, a key Red Sea export route that bypasses the Strait of Hormuz, are the kind of headline oil markets have grown sensitive to since Houthi attacks on the kingdom escalated again this month. Even unverified, the mere suggestion of another strike on Petroline tends to draw a knee-jerk bid in crude given the route's role as a workaround while Hormuz-linked disruptions persist. Absent confirmation from Aramco, the Saudi energy ministry or a wire service, any price reaction attributable specifically to this claim should be treated as rumour-driven positioning rather than a repricing of fundamentals. The bigger, already-confirmed backdrop, last week's wave of Houthi strikes on facilities in Saudi Arabia's south, remains the more material story for oil risk premia this week.

Any confirmation of damage to the pipeline would likely draw a firmer, more durable bid in crude given the route's role as a workaround for Hormuz-linked disruptions, whereas an unverified claim alone would typically be treated as noise rather than a repricing catalyst.

Summary:

Chatter is circulating in oil-focused corners of social media over a possible fresh strike on Saudi Arabia's East-West pipeline, though as of writing there is no confirmation from Aramco, the Saudi energy ministry or major wire services that anything has happened to the line. The claim originates from an account presenting an independent analysis of satellite thermal imagery, arguing that fire radiative power readings above 70 megawatts along the pipeline's route are well beyond what a routine flare or valve leak would produce, and that the heat signature persisted for roughly eight hours, based on a comparison of separate satellite passes.

The account's reasoning also leans on the geography of the anomalies, arguing that Saudi pump stations along the route are normally spaced well apart, whereas the reported heat sources are clustered along a stretch of only a few kilometres, which it says is inconsistent with simultaneous scheduled maintenance. It is worth noting this is one analyst's interpretation of public satellite data, not an assessment from a government agency, Aramco or an established energy intelligence provider, and satellite thermal anomalies of this kind have been misread as attacks before when the underlying cause was industrial activity rather than sabotage.

The timing lends the claim some plausibility on its face. Saudi Arabia experienced a genuine escalation in Houthi attacks just days earlier, when strikes on facilities in the kingdom's south wounded more than 70 people and forced a halt to operations at some energy sites, according to Saudi authorities. The East-West pipeline itself, which carries crude roughly 1,200 kilometres from the Eastern Province to the Red Sea port of Yanbu and functions as a key alternative to Strait of Hormuz shipments, has also been hit in confirmed attacks before, including as recently as April this year.

Until an official source or established wire service corroborates the specific claim, however, it remains market chatter rather than confirmed news. Any price reaction tied directly to this report should be read as speculative positioning around an unverified data point, and traders will likely want to see Aramco, the Saudi energy ministry or independent satellite-monitoring services weigh in before treating it as anything more than that.

il_articles.titre_fr: Attention ci-dessous !  Le cuivre, l'or et l'AUDUSD sont tous en baisse aujourd'hui.
il_articles.contenu_fr:
L’Australie est un exportateur majeur de matières premières dures, notamment d’or et de cuivre. Lorsque les prix des matières premières chutent, la valeur des exportations australiennes peut diminuer, réduisant ainsi le flux de capitaux étrangers dans l’économie australienne. Cela peut peser sur le dollar australien et faire baisser l'AUDUSD.

Le cuivre a également tendance à servir de baromètre pour la croissance mondiale, en particulier pour la demande de la Chine, le plus grand partenaire commercial de l’Australie. Si le cuivre s’effondre, les traders pourraient y voir un avertissement indiquant que la demande mondiale et chinoise s’affaiblit. Cela joue normalement contre le dollar australien, sensible à la croissance.

L’or est un peu plus compliqué car il peut chuter lorsque le dollar américain et les rendements américains augmentent. Un dollar américain plus fort peut exercer une pression sur l'or et le cuivre tout en poussant simultanément l'AUDUSD à la baisse. Dans cette situation, les trois marchés pourraient réagir aux mêmes forces sous-jacentes : un dollar plus fort, des rendements américains plus élevés et un moindre appétit pour le risque.

Les relations ne sont pas parfaites au jour le jour, mais lorsque l’or, le cuivre et l’AUDUSD baissent tous ensemble, les marchés envoient généralement un message cohérent : la demande de matières premières s’affaiblit, les inquiétudes sur la croissance mondiale augmentent ou le dollar américain se renforce – peut-être une combinaison des trois.

L'or, le cuivre et l'AUDUSD sont tous en forte baisse aujourd'hui (or -1,85%, contrats à terme sur cuivre -5,40% et AUDUSD -0,80%). Bien que chaque marché ait sa propre histoire technique, le thème commun est que les niveaux de support clés ont été dépassés. Lorsque plusieurs marchés connexes commencent à confirmer le même message directionnel, les traders ont tendance à y prêter plus attention.

L'or au comptant est passé en dessous d'un important groupe de support proche de 4 355,77 $. Cette zone comprenait la ligne de tendance ascendante, la moyenne mobile sur 100 jours et la moyenne mobile de 200 barres sur le graphique de 4 heures. Lorsque plusieurs outils techniques convergent vers le même prix, ce niveau devient plus important car les traders d’horizons temporels différents le surveillent tous.

La cassure en dessous de ce cluster a donné plus de confiance aux vendeurs et a ouvert la porte vers le point médian de 50 % et la zone de swing proche de 4 315 $ à 4 320 $. C’est la prochaine cible baissière importante. Si les acheteurs ne peuvent pas maintenir la ligne, l'attention se porterait sur 4 282 $, suivi du retracement de 61,8 % près de 4 230 $.

Pour les acheteurs, revenir au-dessus de 4 355,77 $ est désormais l'exigence minimale s'ils veulent reprendre plus de contrôle. En attendant, les vendeurs gardent le contrôle et le support cassé devient une résistance. C'est une leçon clé pour les traders : une fois le support cassé, il devient souvent un plafond définissant le risque en cas de rebond.

Aux États-Unis, les contrats à terme sur le cuivre ont atteint un nouveau sommet hier, mais la dynamique s'est fortement inversée aujourd'hui, le prix ayant chuté de plus de 5 %. Il s’agit d’un changement de ton spectaculaire qui montre à quelle vitesse un mouvement haussier massif peut se dissiper lorsque les acheteurs cessent de soutenir le prix.

La baisse a amené le cuivre en dessous de sa moyenne mobile sur 100 heures à 6,7404 $ et de sa moyenne mobile sur 200 heures à 6,6856 $. Ces cassures ont contribué à accélérer les ventes et ont poussé le prix dans une zone de swing importante proche de 6,516 $. Ce niveau a attiré acheteurs et vendeurs à plusieurs reprises depuis août, ce qui en fait un baromètre important pour le prochain mouvement.

Si la zone des 6,516 $ se maintient, le cuivre pourrait connaître un rebond correctif. Cependant, les acheteurs devraient toujours récupérer les moyennes mobiles cassées sur 200 heures et 100 heures pour réparer les dommages techniques. Sans cela, tout rebond serait considéré comme correctif.

À l’inverse, une cassure prolongée en dessous de 6,516 $ donnerait aux vendeurs une autre victoire et augmenterait le potentiel de baisse vers la moyenne mobile ascendante sur 100 jours proche de 6,382 $. La vitesse de la baisse est importante, mais les traders doivent rester concentrés sur les niveaux. Les marchés rapides peuvent devenir survendus, mais la survente ne signifie pas automatiquement que le plus bas est atteint.

L'AUDUSD a atteint son plus haut niveau depuis mai lors de la séance d'hier, testant la zone de swing supérieure entre 0,7221 et 0,7228. Les acheteurs avaient la possibilité de prolonger le mouvement, mais ils n’ont pas pu maintenir l’élan.

Aujourd'hui, les vendeurs ont poussé le prix en dessous de la moyenne mobile ascendante sur 100 heures, ce qui a déclenché une baisse plus prononcée. La paire est ensuite passée sous la moyenne mobile de 200 heures près de 0,71936 et a traversé la partie inférieure de la zone de swing voisine. Ces cassures ont déplacé plus fermement le biais à court terme en faveur des vendeurs.

Le prix teste actuellement une ligne de tendance haussière proche de 0,7154. Cela devient le prochain niveau clé de définition du risque. Si la ligne de tendance se maintient, les acheteurs pourraient tenter un rebond, mais ils devront récupérer les moyennes mobiles cassées pour reprendre le contrôle.

Une cassure en dessous de 0,7154 ajouterait à la situation technique baissière et inciterait les traders à se tourner vers la zone de swing proche de 0,7139. En dessous, le retracement de 38,2% à 0,71168 deviendrait le prochain objectif important.

La faiblesse du cuivre et de l’or constitue également un obstacle pour le dollar australien. L'Australie est une économie exportatrice majeure de matières premières et l'AUD est souvent traité comme une monnaie de matières premières. En conséquence, une forte baisse des prix des matières premières peut peser sur la monnaie en affaiblissant les perspectives en matière de recettes d’exportation et de croissance économique en général. Cette relation n'est pas parfaite chaque jour de bourse, mais aujourd'hui, les tableaux techniques du cuivre et de l'AUDUSD évoluent dans la même direction baissière.

Dans la vidéo, j'examine de plus près les graphiques de l'or, du cuivre et de l'AUDUSD, j'explique les cassures techniques plus en détail et je décris les niveaux que les acheteurs et les vendeurs devront récupérer (ou franchir) pour prendre la prochaine mesure de contrôle.

Australia is a major exporter of hard commodities, including gold and copper. When those commodity prices fall, the value of Australia’s exports can decline, reducing the flow of foreign money into the Australian economy. That can weigh on the Australian dollar and push the AUDUSD lower.

Copper also tends to act as a barometer for global growth, particularly demand from China—Australia’s largest trading partner. If copper is tumbling, traders may see it as a warning that global and Chinese demand is weakening. That normally works against the growth-sensitive Australian dollar.

Gold is a little more complicated because it can fall when the US dollar and US yields rise. A stronger US dollar can pressure gold and copper while simultaneously pushing the AUDUSD lower. In that situation, all three markets may be reacting to the same underlying forces: a stronger dollar, higher US yields and reduced appetite for risk.

The relationships are not perfect day to day, but when gold, copper and the AUDUSD are all moving lower together, the markets are generally sending a consistent message: commodity demand is weakening, global growth concerns are rising, or the US dollar is gaining strength—perhaps a combination of all three.

Gold, copper and the AUDUSD are all moving sharply lower today (gold -1.85%, Copper futures -5.40% and AUDUSD -0.80%). Although each market has its own technical story, the common theme is that key support levels have been broken. When several related markets begin confirming the same directional message, traders tend to pay closer attention.

Spot gold has moved below an important cluster of support near $4,355.77. That area included the rising trend line, the 100-day moving average and the 200-bar moving average on the 4-hour chart. When several technical tools converge near the same price, that level becomes more important because traders from different time horizons are all watching it.

The break below that cluster gave sellers more confidence and opened the door toward the 50% midpoint and swing area near $4,315–$4,320. That is the next important downside target. If buyers cannot hold the line there, the focus would shift toward $4,282, followed by the 61.8% retracement near $4,230.

For buyers, getting back above $4,355.77 is now the minimum requirement if they are going to take back more control. Until then, the sellers remain in control and the broken support becomes resistance. That is a key lesson for traders: once support is broken, it often becomes a risk-defining ceiling on a rebound.

Copper futures in the US reached another new high just yesterday, but the momentum has reversed sharply today, with the price falling more than 5%. That is a dramatic change in tone and shows how quickly a crowded bullish move can unwind when buyers stop supporting the price.

The decline took copper below both its 100-hour moving average at $6.7404 and its 200-hour moving average at $6.6856. Those breaks helped accelerate the selling and have pushed the price into an important swing area near $6.516. That level has attracted buyers and sellers on several occasions going back to August, making it an important barometer for the next move.

If the $6.516 area holds, copper could see a corrective rebound. However, buyers would still need to reclaim the broken 200-hour and 100-hour moving averages to repair the technical damage. Without that, any rebound would be viewed as corrective.

Conversely, a sustained break below $6.516 would give sellers another victory and increase the downside potential toward the rising 100-day moving average near $6.382. The speed of the decline is important, but traders should remain focused on the levels. Fast markets can become oversold, but oversold does not automatically mean the low is in.

The AUDUSD reached its highest level since May during yesterday’s trading, testing the upper swing area between 0.7221 and 0.7228. Buyers had their shot at extending the move, but they could not keep the momentum going.

Today, sellers pushed the price below the rising 100-hour moving average, which kickstarted a sharper move to the downside. The pair then broke below the 200-hour moving average near 0.71936 and through the lower part of the nearby swing area. Those breaks shifted the short-term bias more firmly in favor of the sellers.

The price is now testing a rising trend line near 0.7154. That becomes the next key risk-defining level. If the trend line holds, buyers could attempt a rebound, but they would need to reclaim the broken moving averages to regain control.

A break below 0.7154 would add to the bearish technical picture and have traders looking toward the swing area near 0.7139. Below that, the 38.2% retracement at 0.71168 would become the next important target.

The weakness in copper and gold is also a headwind for the Australian dollar. Australia is a major commodity-exporting economy, and the AUD is often treated as a commodity currency. As a result, a sharp decline in commodity prices can weigh on the currency by weakening the outlook for export revenues and broader economic growth. That relationship is not perfect on every trading day, but today the technical pictures in copper and the AUDUSD are moving in the same bearish direction.

In the video, I take a closer look at the charts for gold, copper and the AUDUSD, explain the technical breaks in greater detail and outline the levels that buyers and sellers will need to reclaim—or break—to take the next measure of control.

il_articles.contenu:
U.S. wholesale inventories increased strongly in July, while sales rebounded following June’s decline. Inventories grew faster than sales during the month, pushing the inventories-to-sales ratio modestly higher.

Wholesale inventories

The 1.3% rise in inventories was relatively strong. That could indicate wholesalers are rebuilding stocks in anticipation of future demand. However, if inventories continue rising faster than sales, it could also suggest that goods are beginning to accumulate in warehouses.

Wholesale sales

Sales rebounded in July after falling sharply in June. That is a positive sign for business demand, although the 0.8% increase did not fully reverse the previous month’s 2.9% decline.

The annual gain remained strong at 13.0%. However, the data are not adjusted for price changes, meaning some of that increase may reflect higher prices rather than wholesalers selling a proportionately larger quantity of goods.

Inventories-to-sales ratio

The ratio estimates how many months it would take wholesalers to sell their inventories at the current sales pace. July’s reading of 1.20 means wholesalers held inventory equal to approximately1.20 months of sales.

The ratio rose slightly from 1.19 in June because inventories increased faster than sales. Nevertheless, it remained below the 1.28 recorded one year earlier, indicating that inventories are still relatively lean compared with the overall sales pace.

What does it mean?

The July report was mixed but generally showed improving activity. Sales returned to growth, which is encouraging, but inventories rose at a faster rate.

For traders, the key will be whether rising inventories are deliberate—reflecting confidence in future demand—or involuntary because goods are not selling as quickly as expected. The strong annual sales gain and lower year-over-year inventory-to-sales ratio lean toward the more constructive interpretation for now.

Wholesale data are normally not a major market-moving release. However, inventories feed into GDP calculations, while sales offer another view of underlying business demand.

---------------------------------------

U.S. wholesale inventories and wholesale sales provide a look at what is happening between manufacturers and retailers before products reach consumers.

Wholesale salesmeasure the value of goods sold by wholesalers to retailers and other businesses. Rising sales generally suggest demand is improving and businesses may need to order more goods. Falling sales can indicate demand is slowing.

Wholesale inventoriesmeasure the value of goods that wholesalers still have in their warehouses. Rising inventories are not automatically good or bad. The reason they are rising is what matters:

The relationship between the two is captured by theinventories-to-sales ratio. It estimates how many months it would take wholesalers to sell their existing inventories at the current sales pace.

For markets, the report is usually not a major mover by itself, but it helps economists assess economic growth. Inventory building adds to GDP, while inventory reductions can subtract from GDP. However, an inventory increase caused by unexpectedly weak sales is not necessarily a sign of a healthy economy.

For traders, the key is to examine inventories and sales together. Inventories rising alongside strong sales can be constructive. Inventories rising while sales fall may be a warning that demand is weakening.

il_articles.titre_fr: Perspectives boursières Apple : l’iPhone pliable peut-il générer une nouvelle croissance ?
il_articles.contenu_fr:
Apple a dévoilé l'iPhone Duo le 9 septembre, à partir de 1 999 dollars aux États-Unis, et disponible à partir du 23 octobre. Son écran intérieur plus grand permet d'utiliser des applications côte à côte. Annonce d'Apple

L’argument d’investissement est simple : une expérience sensiblement différente pourrait donner aux clients une raison plus forte de remplacer leur téléphone qu’une autre mise à niveau de routine.

Gene Munster a exprimé ce changement de perspective dans son propre commentaire post-événement, affirmant que le duo avait amélioré son évaluation du potentiel de croissance du pliable. Il s’agit là d’une interprétation d’analyste, plutôt que d’une preuve de la demande déjà satisfaite des clients. Analyse de Munster

Ce qui m'intéresse est de savoir si l'espace d'écran supplémentaire devient suffisamment utile pour justifier le prix. Un design attrayant peut attirer l’attention ; des ventes soutenues exigent que les clients voient un avantage dans une utilisation quotidienne.

Non. La part des ventes d’un produit est différente des ventes supplémentaires qu’il crée.

Imaginons un scénario haussier dans lequel les appareils pliables représenteraient à terme 10 % des revenus de l’iPhone. Cela illustre l’ampleur possible de l’entreprise ; il ne s’agit pas de conseils Apple ou d’une prévision liée à une année spécifique.

Apple a déclaré environ 209,6 milliards de dollars de revenus iPhone et 416,2 milliards de dollars de revenus totaux au cours de l'exercice 2025. L'utilisation de cette base historique montre l'ampleur de l'enjeu. États financiers d'Apple pour l'exercice 2025

Illustrations utilisant la même base de revenus pour l’exercice 2025, et non des prévisions de ventes ou des estimations de croissance supplémentaire.

La distinction devient plus claire avec un exemple simple. Supposons que quelqu'un achète un iPhone pliable à 2 000 $ au lieu d'un iPhone conventionnel à 1 300 $. Apple vend un appareil à 2 000 dollars, mais la dépense supplémentaire du client s'élève à 700 dollars, sans tenir compte des remises et des différences de coût.

Cette substitution est appelée cannibalisation, lorsqu'un produit prend les ventes d'un autre produit fabriqué par la même entreprise. Cela peut toujours profiter à Apple si les clients dépensent plus et que le bénéfice supplémentaire est attractif.

De nouveaux clients ajouteraient une source de croissance différente. Des mises à niveau antérieures pourraient également faciliter les ventes à court terme, même si elles pourraient avancer des achats qui autrement auraient lieu plus tard.

L'IA personnelle désigne un logiciel qui peut utiliser des informations pertinentes vous concernant, avec autorisation, pour vous aider à accomplir des tâches. Par exemple, un assistant pourrait trouver les détails d'un voyage dans un message et vous aider à organiser votre calendrier.

Apple affirme que son nouveau Siri peut utiliser le contexte personnel dans les messages, e-mails et autres contenus. Cependant, Siri AI commence en version bêta et Apple indique qu'elle ne sera initialement pas disponible sur iOS dans l'UE. La disponibilité est donc importante lors de l’évaluation de l’opportunité. Détails Siri d’Apple

Un écran plus grand pourrait faciliter la révision des suggestions d’un assistant tout en gardant une autre application ouverte. Mon interprétation est que cela pourrait améliorer l’utilité de l’IA, mais l’écran lui-même ne rend pas l’assistant plus performant.

L’avantage commercial potentiel survient si les gens utilisent régulièrement ces fonctionnalités, préfèrent les appareils Apple en raison de celles-ci ou paient pour des services utiles. Ces résultats nécessitent encore des preuves. Une démonstration convaincante ne constitue pas une source de revenus récurrente.

Demande des clients : observez les tendances des précommandes et des livraisons ainsi que les commentaires sur la production. Les longs délais de livraison peuvent refléter une offre limitée ainsi qu’une forte demande.

Rentabilité : des prix de vente plus élevés ne sont utiles que si les coûts de fabrication, de support et autres génèrent des bénéfices intéressants. La croissance des revenus et la croissance des bénéfices peuvent différer.

Adoption de l’IA : recherchez des fonctionnalités utiles qui parviennent aux clients et deviennent des habitudes. Les dates de lancement, les marchés pris en charge et la fiabilité détermineront le rythme d’adoption.

Attentes de bénéfices : les arguments haussiers se renforcent si les éléments de preuve conduisent les analystes à relever leurs prévisions de bénéfices. Une forte publicité sans amélioration des estimations entraînerait un soutien plus faible.

Pour les traders, les actions AAPL sont l’instrument direct à surveiller. Comparez leurs performances avec le Nasdaq 100 pour juger si les investisseurs récompensent spécifiquement Apple. Sur un graphique, les hauts et les bas du jour du lancement offrent des points de référence pour évaluer si l'enthousiasme initial persiste ; ce ne sont pas des signaux d’entrée automatiques.

Je deviendrais plus constructif si la demande soutenait des attentes de bénéfices plus élevées sans détérioration significative des marges. Une faible demande, des problèmes de production coûteux ou une adoption lente de l’IA affaibliraient ce point de vue. La prochaine preuve utile viendra du comportement des clients et des résultats financiers.

Cet article est à des fins éducatives. Le trading et l’investissement comportent des risques. Les déménageurs Seestock méritent d’être surveillés aujourd’hui.

Apple unveiled theiPhone Duo on September 9, starting at$1,999 in the U.S., with availability fromOctober 23. Its larger inner display supports using apps side by side.Apple’s announcement

The investment argument is straightforward: a noticeably different experience could give customers a stronger reason to replace their phones than another routine upgrade.

Gene Munster expressed that change in perspective in his own post-event commentary, saying the Duo had improved his assessment of the foldable’s growth potential. That is an analyst’s interpretation, rather than evidence of customer demand already delivered.Munster’s analysis

What interests me is whether the extra screen space becomes useful enough to justify the price. Attractive design can generate attention; sustained sales require customers to see a benefit in everyday use.

No. A product’s share of sales is different from the additional sales it creates.

Consider a bullish scenario in which foldables eventually account for10% of iPhone revenue. This illustrates the possible scale of the business; it is not Apple guidance or a forecast tied to a specific year.

Apple reported approximately$209.6 billion in iPhone revenueand$416.2 billion in total revenuein fiscal 2025. Using that historical base shows the scale involved.Apple’s FY2025 financial statements

Illustrations using the same FY2025 revenue base, not sales forecasts or estimates of additional growth.

The distinction becomes clearer with a simple example. Suppose someone buys a$2,000 foldable instead of a $1,300 conventional iPhone. Apple sells a $2,000 device, but the extra customer spending is$700, before considering discounts and differences in cost.

That substitution is calledcannibalization, when one product takes sales from another product made by the same company. It can still benefit Apple if customers spend more and the additional profit is attractive.

New customers would add a different source of growth. Earlier upgrades could also help near-term sales, although they may bring forward purchases that would otherwise happen later.

Personal AI means software that can use relevant information about you, with permission, to help complete tasks. For example, an assistant could find travel details in a message and help organize your calendar.

Apple says its new Siri can use personal context across messages, emails and other content. However, Siri AI begins as a beta, and Apple says it willinitially be unavailable on iOS in the EU. Availability therefore matters when assessing the opportunity.Apple’s Siri details

A larger screen could make it easier to review an assistant’s suggestions while keeping another app open. My interpretation is that this could improve the usefulness of AI, but the screen itself does not make the assistant more capable.

The potential business benefit comes if people use these features regularly, prefer Apple devices because of them, or pay for useful services. Those outcomes still need evidence. A compelling demonstration is not a recurring revenue stream.

Customer demand:Watch preorder and delivery trends alongside production commentary. Long delivery times can reflect limited supply as well as strong demand.

Profitability:Higher selling prices help only if manufacturing, support and other costs leave attractive profits. Revenue growth and profit growth may differ.

AI adoption:Look for useful features reaching customers and becoming habits. Launch dates, supported markets and reliability will shape the pace of adoption.

Earnings expectations:The bullish case strengthens if evidence leads analysts to raise profit forecasts. Strong publicity without improving estimates would offer weaker support.

For traders,AAPL shares are the direct instrument to watch. Compare their performance with the Nasdaq 100 to judge whether investors are rewarding Apple specifically. On a chart, the launch-day high and low offer reference points for assessing whether initial enthusiasm holds; they are not automatic entry signals.

I would become more constructive if demand supports higher earnings expectations without a meaningful deterioration in margins. Weak demand, costly production problems or slow AI adoption would weaken that view. The next useful evidence will come from customer behavior and financial results.

Some bulls in oil (the mainstream) might get angry with me here. Other (bearish) contrarians are gonna love it. Let's get this party going!

Crude oil near $100 is not usually where traders go looking for comfortable short trades. That is exactly what makes this setup interesting.

This potentially contrarian NYMEX Light Crude Oil Futures (CL) trade idea is not simply trying to call the top of the oil rally. Instead, I am watching a cluster of potential reaction and liquidity levels surrounding the psychologically important$100 per barrelarea.

Importantly, crude remains below the proposed entries at the time of this setup. The plan is therefore towait for price to come higher, not chase a short while the market is lower.

The structure also deliberately allows crude to trade above $100, potentially sweep liquidity there, and only then reverse.

Short entry 1: 99.61One-third of the intended position.

Short entry 2: 100.93Another one-third, allowing for a move above the $100 round number.

Short entry 3: 103.05The final one-third, designed for a deeper upside sweep.

Average entry if all three orders fill equally: approximately 101.20

Stop loss: 105.82

If all three entries fill, the initial blended risk is approximately4.62 points per barrel.

If crude never reaches the entries, there is no reason to chase it lower. The trade simply does not activate.

Large round numbers such as$100tend to attract attention.

They can become areas where traders place breakout orders, stops, profit-taking orders and other resting liquidity. Systematic strategies may also react to important psychological prices.

That can occasionally create what traders call aliquidity sweep.

In simple terms, price pushes through an obvious level, triggering orders around it, but then fails to continue and reverses.

That is why this short idea does not depend on crude reversing exactly at $100. The three-entry structure allows for price to trade below and materially above the round number before the idea is either rewarded or invalidated.

First target: 96.17

This is intentionally the closest target. I see it primarily as arisk-mitigation target, rather than necessarily the main bearish objective.

Based on the 101.20 blended entry, TP1 represents approximately1.09R.

Second target: 91.76

The main plan is to reduce the position equally at96.17, 91.76 and 84.86.

If all three entries fill and all three targets are eventually reached, the equivalent blended exit is approximately90.93, producing a blended reward-to-risk ratio of about2.22R.

One approach traders may consider is moving the stop on the remaining position to theiractual average entryand cancelling any higher short-entry orders that were never filled.

If all three original entries had already filled, that breakeven reference would be approximately101.20.

Crude could move straight through $100, continue through the proposed entry zone and keep rising.

That is why the predefined105.82 stopmatters. It defines where this particular short thesis should be considered wrong rather than turning a planned trade into an open-ended bet against the oil rally.

The idea is not that crude "must" top near $100.

The rise in long-term bond yields is being blamed on a growing list of factors, but there is a much simpler explanation sitting in plain sight:oil prices are the main driver of the rise in long-term yields, and the Iran war is the reason oil is rising.

Brent crude has pushed back above $100 a barrel as the US-Iran conflict escalated, while the 10-year Treasury yield has climbed above 4.8%, its highest level since 2023.

The key transmission mechanism is inflation. An oil price shock does not stay confined to the energy market. Higher crude prices feed into gasoline, diesel, transportation and production costs. If the shock persists, investors begin to worry that inflation will remain higher for longer, especially without a central bank's response.

That matters enormously for long-duration bonds. If the inflation outlook deteriorates, investors demand a higher yield to compensate for the loss of purchasing power and the greater uncertainty around future interest rates.

That is why the relationship between oil and long-term yields matters more right now than many of the other headlines competing for attention or suiting the price action. Below you can clearly see the tight correlation between the US 10y Treasury yield (red) and WTI crude oil (blue).

In the current context, oil and bonds are   the same story. The escalation of the Iran conflict has  increased the risk of further and longer disruption through the Strait of Hormuz. As a reminder, the waterway normally carries roughly a fifth of global oil and gas supplies.

Brent closed above $100 on Wednesday for the first time since July, while physical oil prices have also surged as buyers compete for alternative barrels. S&P Global reported that Dated Brent jumped to $114.26 on September 9, highlighting how tight the physical market has become.

This is where the bond market comes in. If the war pushes oil higher, the market has to reassess the inflation outlook. If inflation expectations rise, expectations for monetary policy can shift. Even if the Federal Reserve ultimately looks through a temporary energy shock, the market still has to price the possibility that the shock becomes persistent. That puts upward pressure on long-term yields.

The Treasury's buyback programme is important, but it is not the primary explanation for the broader move in yields. TheTreasury announced plans to repurchase up to $6 billion of longer-dated debt. The idea is to improve liquidity and support the long end of the curve. Yet the 10-year yield continued to rise, reaching levels not seen since 2023. Much of that was because the announcement disappointed expectations, as there were talks of $10 billion or even 12$ billion buybacks, but the main reason is inflation concerns.

The buyback can influence the mechanics of the bond market but it cannot make $100 oil disappear. Long-term yields have been rising across the globe and the only fixes for that are either central bank tightening (which could eventually trigger a recession) or an end to the Iran war.

For now, oil is the signal. Everything else is just noise.

That company-specific debate is happening against a difficult market backdrop. Brent crude remains above$100, the U.S. 10-year Treasury yield is around4.84%, and investors are waiting for Thursday's U.S. producer price inflation report at08:30 ET. Higher oil prices and bond yields can make investors less willing to pay high valuations for future growth.

The common thread is simple:being connected to AI or beating the latest earnings estimate is no longer enough. Investors increasingly want evidence that growth can translate into better future economics.

Meta shares gained more than6% Wednesdayafter the company introducedMuse, a personal AI agent designed to go beyond answering questions and actually perform tasks such as booking travel, filling out forms and working across connected apps.

That matters because investors have spent much of the AI boom asking how companies investing enormous sums in AI infrastructure will eventually make money from it.

Muse gives Meta a more tangible consumer product to place against that spending.

The bullish interpretation is not simply that Meta has "more AI." It is that the company may have another product capable of increasing engagement, strengthening its ecosystem and potentially creating subscription, commerce or advertising opportunities.

What traders could watch Thursday:whether Wednesday's strong META move attracts further buyers or whether investors quickly take profits after the initial Muse enthusiasm.

The longer-term question remains much bigger:Can Meta convert AI spending into products people use frequently enough to produce meaningful financial returns?

ServiceTitan provides almost the opposite lesson.

The company reported quarterly revenue of$292.8 million, up 21% from a year earlier, while generating more than$50 million of non-GAAP free cash flow. Those numbers were stronger than expected.

But ServiceTitan forecast third-quarter revenue of$285 million to $287 million, compared with a Wall Street estimate around $288 million. Changes involving its AI-linked Max product are also expected to temporarily delay some revenue recognition. The stock subsequently fell around30%.

For newer investors, this can initially look irrational.

Why would a stock fall so much after beating earnings?

Because stocks trade largely onfuture expectations, not just the quarter that has already finished.

ServiceTitan entered the report with investors expecting rapid future growth. Even a relatively modest reduction in those expectations can cause a major valuation reset when a stock is priced for strong expansion.

What traders could watch Thursday:whether the large decline begins attracting buyers near Wednesday's lows or whether sellers remain in control despite the much lower share price.

Navan presents another variation on the same theme.

Quarterly revenue increased35% to $232.8 million, beating expectations, while the company also raised its full-year revenue outlook to$927 million to $933 million.

Yet shares fell roughly17% after hours.

One reason is expenses.

Operating expenses increased about46% to $200.2 million, while the GAAP operating loss widened to $25.6 million. Management attributed some of the increase to sales commissions and AI investment.

That creates a useful question for growth-stock investors:

Is the company spending today to create much greater profits tomorrow, or is maintaining rapid growth becoming increasingly expensive?

A business can produce impressive revenue growth while still disappointing shareholders if expenses rise even faster.

What traders could watch Thursday:whether the after-hours decline survives once regular-session liquidity returns. A substantial recovery would suggest investors view the cost increase as manageable. Continued selling would indicate that profitability concerns remain more important.

Cloudflare provides the positive counterpoint.

The company recently introduced a vulnerability discovery and remediation service that uses OpenAI Daybreak models, includingGPT-5.6 Cyber, together with Cloudflare's security and network data to identify and help remediate software vulnerabilities.

The important distinction is that investors can see a relatively direct connection between the AI technology and a commercial cybersecurity product.

My Cloudflare's daily chart below shows the strong recovery above $300 on increased volume, with the August all-time high near $332 becoming the next major technical area to watch.

Cloudflare produced a strong bullish daily move, with NET closing at$314.18, up 10.5%, after reaching$317.55intraday.

More importantly, the advance came with4.78 million shares of volume, roughly54% above the supplied recent volume average. That gives the move stronger confirmation than a similar rally occurring on light participation.

The advance also repairs much of the weakness from early September.

NET has pushed decisively back above the$300-$303 area, while closing relatively close to the session high. Attention can therefore shift toward the August peak around$332.22, roughly 5.7% above the latest close.

That does not mean NET must reach it.

The more useful question is whether buyers canhold the newly reclaimed arearather than immediately surrendering Wednesday's breakout.

Momentum strengthened alongside price.

The supplied RSI reading increased from roughly48.8 to 58.6and crossed above its RSI-based moving average.

For traders, the important point is not the indicator by itself. It is thatprice, momentum and trading volume improved at the same time.

That combination provides stronger evidence than a rally driven by only one of those factors.

The$300-$303 areanow becomes particularly interesting.

If NET can stay above it, the recent pullback increasingly looks repaired and the$332 arearemains a logical next reference.

If the stock quickly falls back below $300, particularly with stronger selling volume, Wednesday's breakout becomes less convincing.

Educational takeaway:Volume can help traders judge the quality of a breakout. A strong price move accompanied by unusually high trading volume suggests broader participation. It does not guarantee that the rally will continue, but it usually provides more supporting evidence than price movement alone.

American Eagle offers one of Thursday's best lessons inearnings quality.

The retailer reported record quarterly revenue of$1.38 billion, while total comparable sales increased 6%. But performance differed sharply between its brands:Aerie comparable sales rose 19%, while American Eagle comparable sales fell 1%.

There is another important detail.

American Eagle received$196 million of tariff refunds, with a net benefit of approximately$161 million to operating incomeduring the quarter.

Shares fell around 10% after hours.

This is why investors should not stop reading at "EPS beat."

A better question is:

How much of the earnings improvement came from the underlying business, and how much came from something unlikely to repeat?

One-time gains can make a quarter look much stronger without necessarily improving the company's long-term earning power.

Signet Jewelers was one of Wednesday's strongest winners.

The company reported2.2% same-store sales growth, raised its fiscal-year guidance and expanded its share repurchase authorization. It also said it intends to enter into a$125 million accelerated share repurchaseagreement.

The combination matters: improving operations, better management expectations and capital being returned to shareholders can reinforce one another.

CooperCompanies produced a much less favorable share-price reaction.

The company reported quarterly revenue of$1.066 billion, up only 1% year over year, while its fourth-quarter guidance pointed to organic revenue growth of just0%-2%. CooperVision is expected to show organic growth between-2% and 0%in the fourth quarter.

Again, investors are looking forward rather than backward.

The most useful lesson from this group is not that AI stocks are bullish or software stocks are bearish.

The market appears to be becomingmore selective.

Investors are asking harder questions:

Meta:Can AI create products consumers actually use?

Cloudflare:Can AI become a product customers pay for?

Navan:Is AI-supported growth producing enough operating leverage?

ServiceTitan:Are future growth expectations still high enough to justify the valuation?

American Eagle:How much of reported profit comes from the underlying business?

Signet:Are better results strong enough for management to raise expectations and return more capital?

Those are very different questions, but they share one idea:

The quality of growth increasingly matters as much as the growth itself.

For Thursday's U.S. session,META, TTAN, NAVN and NETstand out.

META tests whether enthusiasm around a tangible new AI product can continue. TTAN tests whether a 30% valuation reset is enough to attract dip buyers. NAVN tests whether investors can look beyond sharply rising costs. NET tests whether Wednesday's high-volume breakout can hold above the reclaimed$300-$303area.

Traders should also keep the macro environment in view. Oil above $100, elevated Treasury yields and Thursday's PPI release could change risk appetite across growth stocks even when the individual company story remains intact.

The setups above are scenarios to monitor, not predictions of what these stocks must do next. Technical levels, earnings reactions and after-hours prices can fail or reverse quickly, particularly around major economic data.Trade or invest at your own risk and use appropriate risk controls.

What else can stock investors and traders watch today?

Oracle reports its fiscal first-quarter 2027 results after the US market close today, putting the software and cloud infrastructure giant back in the spotlight as investors try to determine whether its aggressive AI investment cycle is translating into sustainable growth.

Wall Street expects adjusted EPS of around $1.75 and revenue of about $19.1 billion, which would represent roughly 28% y/y revenue growth. But for this report, the headline EPS number may not be the most important figure. Investors are likely to focus on Oracle's cloud growth, the conversion of its enormous backlog into actual revenue, capital spending and how the company plans to finance its AI infrastructure buildout.

Consensus estimates put Oracle's quarterly revenue at approximately $19.1 billion to $19.13 billion, with adjusted EPS around $1.74-$1.75. That would represent a substantial acceleration from the same quarter last year.

The more important question, however, is whether Oracle can continue delivering the extremely rapid cloud growth that has become central to its investment story.

Oracle's latest guidance called for:

Those targets provide investors with an important benchmark for judging tonight's numbers and the outlook.

Oracle is best known as one of the world's largest enterprise software and database companies. Its products are used by businesses and governments to manage databases, financial systems, human resources, supply chains and other critical operations.

But the company has been undergoing a major transformation. Rather than relying primarily on traditional on-premise software, Oracle has been pushing aggressively into cloud computing, particularly Oracle Cloud Infrastructure (OCI). OCI provides computing, storage and other infrastructure that companies can use to run applications and increasingly AI workloads.

Oracle also sells cloud-based applications through businesses such as Fusion and NetSuite. This shift matters because cloud infrastructure is growing much faster than Oracle's traditional software businesses.

In fiscal 2026, Oracle's total revenue increased 17% to $67.4 billion, while cloud revenue jumped 39% to $34 billion. Cloud infrastructure revenue was particularly strong, rising 77% to $18.1 billion. The AI boom has accelerated that transition.

Perhaps the most eye-catching number heading into the earnings report is Oracle's remaining performance obligations (RPO). RPO reached $638 billion at the end of fiscal Q4, up $85 billion from the previous quarter and 363% from a year earlier. RPO represents contracted revenue that Oracle expects to recognize in the future.

A large portion of the recent increase has come from major AI-related contracts. Oracle said that prepaid and customer-supplied hardware associated with its large AI contracts totaled $75 billion, helping reduce the amount of capital it needs to raise to build the required data centers.

On one side, the backlog suggests enormous future demand for Oracle's infrastructure. On the other, investors need to see Oracle actually build the capacity required to convert those contracts into revenue. That makes backlog conversion and data-center capacity two of the most important things to watch.

OCI has become the centrepiece of Oracle's AI story. Cloud infrastructure revenue grew 93% y/y in Q4, reaching $5.8 billion. Investors will want to see whether that extraordinary growth rate can continue and whether Oracle maintains its guidance for roughly 58%-64% total cloud growth. A strong headline beat without equally strong cloud growth could therefore be less impressive than it initially appears.

Oracle is spending enormous amounts of money to build data-center capacity. The company reported negative free cash flow of $23.7 billion in fiscal 2026, despite generating $32 billion of operating cash flow.

The issue for investors is not simply whether AI demand exists. It is whether the returns from that demand will ultimately justify the infrastructure spending required to serve it. That makes management commentary on capital expenditure, data-center construction and customer demand particularly important.

Oracle's AI expansion comes with a significant financing requirement. The company raised $43 billion of debt and $5 billion of equity in fiscal 2026. It has said it expects to raise approximately $40 billion in fiscal 2027 through a combination of debt and equity, including a previously announced $20 billion at-the-market equity issuance.

That creates another key question for investors: how aggressively can Oracle continue expanding without putting excessive pressure on its balance sheet and cash flows? This concern has become particularly important because Oracle's stock has fallen sharply from its 2025 peak despite the enormous growth in its AI backlog.

The $638 billion RPO figure is impressive, but investors will increasingly want evidence that those contracts are moving through the pipeline and becoming recognized revenue. Management's commentary around timing, data-center capacity and customer deployments will be important. A growing backlog is bullish. A growing backlog that cannot be monetized quickly enough to justify the investment required to fulfill it is a different story.

Oracle is no longer simply a traditional software company. It has become an important part of the market's broader AI infrastructure trade. Oracle sits between major AI customers and the physical infrastructure required to run increasingly demanding workloads. Its results therefore provide investors with another data point on the strength of enterprise AI spending and the economics of the massive data-center buildout.

A strong Oracle report could reinforce the broader view that AI infrastructure demand remains powerful. That could have implications for other cloud, semiconductor and data-center names. Conversely, weak cloud growth, disappointing guidance or signs that financing and capital spending are becoming constraints could revive concerns about whether the AI infrastructure boom is generating sufficient returns. That is why today's report matters beyond ORCL itself.

Oracle's earnings arrive at a particularly important moment for the AI trade. The company has enormous contracted demand, rapidly growing cloud infrastructure revenue and exposure to some of the world's biggest AI customers. At the same time, it is spending heavily, raising substantial amounts of capital and carrying a much larger financial burden than it did before its AI expansion. The market therefore has two competing narratives to price tonight.

Bull case:Oracle's cloud infrastructure growth continues to accelerate, its enormous backlog converts into revenue, and today's heavy investment creates a much larger and more profitable business over time.

Risk case:AI demand remains strong, but Oracle's spending and financing requirements rise faster than its ability to turn that demand into cash flow.

For traders, the reaction may therefore depend less on whether Oracle simply beats the $1.75 EPS consensus and more on what management says about cloud growth, AI capacity, capital spending, financing and backlog conversion. The earnings number is only the starting point. The guidance and the cash-flow story could determine where Oracle goes next.

ORCL is currently trading around $161, which is more than 53% lower from its all-time peak around $345. The stock has been slowly recovering losses, but there's still a very long way to go to reach new record highs.

For the buyers, we have a nice support area around the $140 level and  an upward trendline adding technical confluence. A spike into the support could provide a dip-buying opportunity to position into the $250 level next. For the sellers, a break below the support could extend the drop into the 2026 low around the $115 level.
